items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: although as I say, I admired both Miles and Coltrane. I have all their records.

ctx.x: I had that ready because you and I share that. I think he’s the tops. He just —

Absolutely. Absolutely. And you know back when I was — ’57, ’58, ’59 of course, when all those great Miles Davis Sextet albums were recorded I used to — I have told people, I’ve told kids when I teach to try to explain the difference between those three soloists: Miles Davis, John Coltrane and Cannonball Adderley. You know Miles, and these are generalizations of course, but you know it’s more or less true, that Miles was very sophisticated and played — you know he held back a lot. He’d go [scats]. And you’d just…
And he was so effective as a band leader and a speaker. I mean he just was so hip, he’d stand up there and, I got to see him a number of times and I just was so sucked into him.
